title: Conjectural formula for minimal permutation representations of general linear groups
statement:
Let $q \geq 5$ be an odd prime power, let $g=\gcd(n,q-1)$, and write the prime factorization of $g$ as $g=p_1^{r_1}\cdots p_s^{r_s}$. For a natural number $m$, write

$$
m=p_1^{a_1}\cdots p_s^{a_s}q_1^{b_1}\cdots q_t^{b_t}
$$

with the $p_i$ and $q_j$ distinct, and define

$$
m_{n,q}=p_1^{a_1}\cdots p_s^{a_s},\qquad T_{n,q}(m)=\sum_{i=1}^{t}q_i^{b_i}.
$$

Here $p({\rm GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q))$ and $p({\rm SL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q))$ denote the minimal faithful permutation degrees. **General linear group conjecture.** If $g=1$, then

$$
p({\rm GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q))=\frac{q^n-1}{q-1}+T_{n,q}(q-1),
$$

whereas if $g>1$, then

$$
p({\rm GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q))=p({\rm SL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q))+T_{n,q}(q-1).
$$

These formulas predict the additional contribution from the factors of $q-1$ not appearing in $g$; the conjecture is presented as an explicit formula for general linear groups, with no resolution supplied in the source.
source_name: Neelima Borade and Ramin Takloo-Bighash, “Minimal permutation representations for linear groups”, arXiv:2103.06346 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.06346

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).
